text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Sheffield United and Liverpool at Bramall Lane!

Being thumped 5-0 by Burnley heralded both the sacking of Paul Heckingbottom and Chris Wilder's Sheffield United comeback, and the latter's Bramall Lane return comes with his boyhood club rooted to the foot of the Premier League table.
The Blades have a four-point deficit to 17th-placed Luton Town, having won just once and failed to keep a single clean sheet in the league this season.
Following five successive top-flight defeats to Liverpool, the Yorkshire side today seek a first win over the Reds since 2003.

Liverpool extended their perfect home record with a remarkable 4-3 victory over Fulham last weekend, when Trent Alexander-Arnold's 87th-minute strike secured the Reds' 11th win from 11 games at Anfield.
As a result, Jurgen Klopp's men sit second in the Premier League standings, five points below leaders Arsenal.

However, only one of Liverpool's last six away games has ended in success - a 2-1 EFL Cup win away to Bournemouth - and each of their 10 road trips this season has seen them concede at least one goal.
Wilder starts his second spell in charge of Sheffield United without striker Oli McBurnie, who is suspended after his red card against Burnley.
In one of five changes, Osula replaces McBurnie up front; Bogle, Vinicius, McAtee and Brooks all come in too.
George Baldock succumbed to a hamstring injury on Saturday, while Chris Basham, John Egan and ex-Liverpool forward Rhian Brewster are among those still sidelined.
Joel Matip may have joined several team-mates in Liverpool's treatment room folllowing the win over Fulham, but Ibrahima Konate is now ready to replace him in the visitors' starting XI.
Endo starts after scoring as a substitute last weekend, while Gakpo and Gomez are also promoted.
Alisson, Diogo Jota, Andrew Robertson, Thiago Alcantara and Stefan Bajcetic all remain unavailable.
The players are out on the pitch at a packed Bramall Lane, and kick-off is now just moments away!
Liverpool kick off, and we are under way in Sheffield!
Hamer delivers a curling free-kick into the box from the right, but two late-arriving team-mates can't quite get a boot on it near the back post and the ball whistles wide.
After a clumsy challenge by Vinicius in central midfield, Mac Allister is left writhing around on the turf in apparent agony.
Liverpool's medical staff rush on, and the game comes to a halt while he receives treatment.

With an average age of 24 years and 239 days, United’s starting XI tonight is the second-youngest they have ever named for a Premier League game, only ahead of their final day line-up of the 1992-93 campaign versus Chelsea (24 years 210 days).
Cautiously, Mac Allister returns to his feet with some help, then jogs gently towards the touchline.
It seems like he'll be fit enough to continue, but the game resumes with Liverpool momentarily a man down.
Mac Allister is back in the thick of things in midfield, as the game searches for some rhythm.
After Diaz dashes up the left wing and dinks over a cross to the back post, Salah slashes his first-time shot well over the crossbar.
Causing havoc in the hosts' penalty area, Szoboszlai sends over a dipping corner from the left, which Robinson has to head over his own crossbar.
Liverpool can't make anything of the second corner-kick though.

SAVE! Kelleher keeps Liverpool level! A counter-attack by the Blades ends with McAtee being set free past Gomez and into the box, and the young midfielder's side-foot volley from 10 yards forces the Irish goalkeeper into a smart stop at close range!
Gomez holds onto the ball for too long on the left wing, then sends a pass towards Diaz straight out of play.
It's not quite clicking for Liverpool at the moment - though it's worth remembering both teams have made several personnel changes today.
On the left byline, Diaz latches on to a searching ball up from the back, then cuts it back for Gakpo on the edge of the area.
However, the latter can't get a shot away, and Liverpool's attack ultimately falters.
A collision between United goalkeeper Foderingham and captain Ahmedhodzic sees the action temporarily brought to a halt, but both are soon back on their feet and play then continues.
After a scuffed cross by Gomez earns Liverpool a corner-kick, Van Dijk reaches the ball first but sees his tame effort tipped over by Foderingham.
Then, the follow-up set-piece results in Mac Allister driving a 20-yard shot well over the crossbar.
Another Liverpool corner is cleared, before they recycle the ball and Konate directs a weak header towards goal, causing Foderingham to dive across and make a regulation save.
The visitors are looking a little more cohesive now, but are just lacking some sharpness in the final third.
With 79 per cent possession so far - and 87 per cent over the past 10 minutes - Liverpool have certainly established themselves as the dominant force at Bramall Lane.
United won't mind playing without the ball, though, and are still very much in this game.
Konate's sweeping crossfield ball towards Diaz on the left is cut out by Bogle, who has to concede another corner-kick.
Following the Reds' latest set-piece situation, Hamer ultimately clears the ball to safety.
A promising move by the home side is stopped in its tracks when Osula tries to release Archer into the area, only to see his team-mate flagged for offside.
It's still one-way traffic at Bramall Lane, with Liverpool patiently probing for an opening, and Sheffield United sitting back and hoping to counter.
Can Klopp's men make their dominance pay before the break? They'll perhaps need to be a bit more precise with their final ball.
Archer sees the ball stolen by Salah deep in United territory, then the Liverpool winger turns into the area and hits the deck under challenge by Vinicius.
The game goes on, though, after the VAR completes a quick check for a possible penalty.
Endo receives the game's first booking for a needless foul on Trusty.
He'll have to tread carefully now.
Ahmedhodzic heads straight at Kelleher from inside the area, following a long throw hurled into the box from out on the left.
Such deliveries could be United's best route to scoring today.
LIVERPOOL LEAD! Alexander-Arnold's corner from the right falls into the area, where Gakpo misses it with a leap and the ball drops into Van Dijk's path.
The Liverpool skipper then side-foots the ball past Foderingham from 10 yards out, picking out the bottom-left corner! It's 1-0 to the visitors, who fully merit their advantage.
Alexander-Arnold's set-piece mastery prevails again, as his corner is swung over from the right and finally lands at the feet of goalscorer Van Dijk.
Another Alexander-Arnold corner finds Van Dijk, but this time the Dutch defender is off-target with his effort.
He rises highest in the box, but heads over the crossbar from close range.

Liverpool are pushing for a second goal before half-time: the increasingly influential Alexander-Arnold tries a rather hopeful shot from outside the box, but sees it sail high over the top, accompanied by jeers from the home fans.
Liverpool have now attempted the last five shots, with United's last attempt at goal taken by Archer as long ago as the 18th minute.
Hampered by the ball being a little behind him, Salah shoots tamely at Foderingham from the right side of the area, following a throughball by Szoboszlai.
There are to be at least six minutes of stoppage time at the end of this first half, as Mac Allister's early injury held up proceedings for quite a while.
Wilder stands impassively on the touchline as McAtee sends a 25-yard free-kick well over the crossbar and into the stand behind Kelleher's goal.
It seems as if the home side are going to end this half goalless.

SHARP STOP! With great confidence and technique, Mac Allister controls the ball and then shoots in one motion, testing Foderingham from just inside the box! The goalkeeper reaches up and tips the volleyed effort over for another Liverpool corner-kick!
HALF-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 0-1 LIVERPOOL

Although short of both rhythm and fluency, Liverpool still lead at Bramall Lane, as their total dominance of the ball finally paid when captain Van Dijk turned the ball home from close range following an Alexander-Arnold corner.

Chris Wilder's homecoming started brightly enough from a Sheffield United point of view, with McAtee testing Kelleher early on, but the Blades have rarely threatened since and may need to have a rethink during the break.
Can the hosts eke out more possession during the second half, or could a set-piece get them back into the game?

Continuing his purple patch by setting up Liverpool's opener today, Alexander-Arnold now has 75 assists in all competitions for the Merseyside club; since his debut in October 2016, only Kevin De Bruyne (129) and Mohamed Salah (80) have racked up more for Premier League teams.
With absences reducing Klopp's options at the moment, the England star is increasingly influential - he has also created more chances (three) than any other player in this game.
The home side kick off, and we are back under way at Bramall Lane!
Brooks dances inside from the left, then whips in a dangerous low ball for Osula in the area.
Van Dijk is alert, though, and guides it away for a corner, which ultimately comes to nothing.
Mac Allister is brought down again - this time by Bogle's ill-timed tackle - and once more he stays on the turf.
Eventually, it is decided that the medics won't be required, and the referee gestures to his watch as if to assure Sheffield United this time will be added on at the end of the game.

While United have picked up just one point from seven games after trailing at the break this season, Liverpool are unbeaten in their last 129 Premier League matches when leading at half-time - a streak dating back to December 2016.
Gakpo and Salah work a few feet of space on the right, before the latter feeds Alexander-Arnold's overlapping run with a throughball.
A deflection then carries the ball into the side-netting for another Liverpool corner.
SUPER SAVE! Salah is denied by Foderingham! The goalkeeper reaches up and gets a strong hand to the Liverpool winger's powerful volley, tipping the ball over his crossbar! That keeps his team in it!
For the third time today, Mac Allister drops to the deck, and it looks like the Liverpool midfielder cannot continue.
He took a heavy blow during the first half, and it seems to have taken its toll.
Klopp's injury woes continue.
Due to injury, Mac Allister is withdrawn from Liverpool's midfield, and Jones jogs on to replace him.
Supporting his back three, Bogle chases back and halts an incisive sprint down the left flank by Diaz, who is on the brink of United's box.
That's excellent defending from the wing-back.
For deliberately clipping Archer midway through the Liverpool half, Konate becomes the second Liverpool player booked today.
Mirroring events in the first half, Liverpool have had a 79 per cent share of possession since the interval - but they've yet to find a decisive second goal.
Until they do, a flicker of hope remains for the hosts.
Salah's throughball for Jones on the right is delayed just too long, and the latter is caught narrowly offside.
It looks like Liverpool are going to make a couple of changes now.
Klopp introduces fresh legs for the closing stages of this game.
First, Diaz makes way for Nunez in Liverpool's front three.
Salah's shift is also over; Elliott is sent on to replace him.
Konate takes a slight blow to the head, causing a brief delay, but the French defender is soon fit enough to continue and the game goes on, moving closer towards its conclusion.
Liverpool may have lost just one of their last 12 Premier League away games, but they’re also winless in their last four.
Klopp will be keen to close this one out, as dropping points here could prove a costly slip-up in the title race.
Gakpo's chipped pass towards the right byline is too strong for Elliott, and the ball rolls frustratingly out of play.
There's no doubt that Liverpool have been far from their fluent best - Klopp's touchline ranting would suggest that, too - but they still lead with less than 20 minutes of the 90 to play.
Wilder decides to shake things up a little, making a double substitution.
First, Brooks is replaced by Fleck.
Traore is also sent on, with Osula making way.
GOOD SAVE! Alexander-Arnold slips a lovely low ball through to Nunez, who angles his run towards the right corner of the area.
He fails to get enough height on his shot, though, and the on-rushing Foderingham makes another smart stop on the edge of his six-yard box!
From the left, Robinson hurls another long throw into the Liverpool area, but it bounces twice without a Sheffield United touch before being cleared to safety by the visitors.

After a conference between Szoboszlai and Alexander-Arnold, the latter's free-kick delivery into the area is initially cleared away from danger, but Liverpool reclaim the ball and start to build more pressure.
The Blades just cannot get out of their own half here.
Having petulantly kicked the ball way after running it out of play on the right, Nunez is shown a yellow card by the referee.
A misplaced pass towards Elliott sees Nunez thwarted, after a charging run had opened up some space through the centre of Sheffield United's midfield.
The substitute's touch has been lacking since arriving from the bench.
Both managers make a further change.
First, Liverpool take off the ineffective Gakpo, to be replaced by his compatriot Gravenberch.
Vinicius is withdrawn, and Norwood comes into the hosts' midfield.
The Bramall Lane faithful are in uproar after an apparent shove by Konate on McAtee goes unpunished.
The latter is sent sprawling in the Liverpool area, but neither the referee nor VAR are interested.
Trusty is now withdrawn, and Lowe comes on to replace him.
Archer volleys the ball into the ground from near the penalty spot, then sees it loop up harmlessly over Kelleher's crossbar.
United claim a corner-kick, but the referee gives the decision Liverpool's way.
An ugly lunge on Szoboszlai earns Norwood a yellow card - that means he'll miss this weekend's clash with Brentford through suspension.
In the second of at least six added minutes at the end of this match, Sheffield United have committed a few more bodies forward in search of a late equaliser.
That leaves some space for Liverpool to exploit, but the hosts have to go for it now.

SZOBOSZLAI SEALS IT! Liverpool finally secure victory, it's 2-0 to the Reds! Nunez steals the ball in midfield, then zips a pass across the box for Szoboszlai, who kills it with his first touch before side-footing home from close range! Foderingham is left helpless, and that wraps up all three points for the visitors!
Nunez is perhaps fortunate not to concede a free-kick when winning the ball back on the right flank, but he then delivers a precise pass for Szoboszlai to convert from close in.
Due to dissent after Liverpool's second goal, Bogle is booked.
FULL-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 0-2 LIVERPOOL
Moving back within two points of Arsenal at the Premier League summit, below-par Liverpool see off struggling Sheffield United and secure a 2-0 victory with goals late in either half.
Van Dijk and Szoboszlai both converted coolly from close range to make the Reds' dominance of possession pay, while their hosts battled bravely without posing much threat in the final third.

This result extends Liverpool's unbeaten run in the top flight to its eighth game, and they will aim to prolong such a streak on Saturday, when in the second of three straight away fixtures they visit Selhurst Park to meet Crystal Palace.
Meanwhile, the beaten Blades host Brentford this weekend, with Wilder hoping to get off the mark in his second spell as United boss.
That's all from Bramall Lane today, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!
